verdict.rationale: AnythingLLM ships a first-party developer API, published as a 67-path OpenAPI 3.0 spec, for reading, writing and updating the instance, and for managing, embedding into and chatting with workspaces. That covers much of the UI's core functionality. However, nothing documents or verifies that every UI capability (e.g., agent flows, admin controls, white-labeling) is reachable through the API, and it is only available on self-hosted or desktop instances. Missing for 10: an explicit or verified UI-to-API parity mapping, evidence of API coverage for agent flows/skills and admin settings, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: API endpoints that enable programmatic reading, writing, and updating of your AnythingLLM instance.
AnythingLLM supports a full developer API that you can use to manage, update, embed, and even chat with your workspaces
